ALGER, 26/06/2026 (Algeria Tech) — Le mi: ALGER, 06/26/2026 (Algeria Tech) — The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications has launched an exceptional campaign to strengthen network stability and service quality for telecom operators during the 2026 peak summer season.
Mobilisation des opérateurs télécoms pou: Mobilization of telecom operators for an uninterrupted summer
Le ministère de la Poste et des Télécomm: The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications announced this Thursday, June 26, 2026, the launch of a targeted operation aimed at ensuring network stability and service quality for operators Mobilis SA, Djezzy, and Ooredoo during the summer period. This initiative is part of a national plan to prevent disruptions, particularly during the months of July and August, when demand for connectivity and mobile services reaches historical peaks. The three operators have been requested to strengthen existing infrastructures, especially in coastal and touristic wilayas, where user concentration is at its highest.
Les mesures incluent l’optimisation des: Measures include optimizing cell tower capacities, deploying temporary solutions to absorb overloads, and setting up dedicated teams to intervene in the event of outages or network saturation. According to the latest data from the Post and Electronic Communications Regulatory Authority (ARPCE), mobile traffic in Algeria is expected to exceed a 125% penetration rate in 2026, with over 35 million active subscribers. The wilayas of Béjaïa, Oran, Tipaza, and Annaba, as main tourist destinations, will be prioritized in this system.
Cette mobilisation s’inscrit dans une st: This mobilization is part of a broader strategy for the resilience of the telecommunications sector, an essential pillar of the Algerian digital economy. Network disruptions during the summer period can have major economic repercussions, particularly for the tourism and online services sectors, which rely heavily on connectivity. In 2025, estimated losses due to network outages during the summer holidays had reached nearly 5 billion Algerian dinars (DZD), according to internal ARPCE reports. Strengthening service quality during these critical periods would not only limit these losses but also improve Algeria's image as a connected tourist destination.
Sur le plan technologique, cette opérati: Technological-wise, this operation highlights the challenges related to adapting infrastructures to the growing needs of users. With a mobile penetration rate exceeding 120% and exponential demand for mobile data, operators must invest massively in the modernization of their networks. The 2030 digital plan, launched by the authorities, also provides for an investment of 1,200 billion DZD for the development of telecom infrastructures, including the widespread rollout of 5G and the improvement of coverage in rural and border areas.
Contexte du secteur TIC algérien: Context of the Algerian ICT sector
Le secteur des technologies de l’informa: The Information and Communication Technology (ICT) sector in Algeria is experiencing sustained growth, driven by increased demand for digital services and an ambitious national strategy. By 2026, the mobile penetration rate in Algeria is expected to reach 125%, with more than 35 million active subscribers, according to ARPCE projections. This figure places Algeria among the most advanced African countries in terms of mobile connectivity, behind South Africa and Morocco. Meanwhile, the number of internet subscribers now exceeds 30 million, with an annual growth rate of 8%, primarily driven by the adoption of broadband plans and OTT (Over-The-Top) services.
L’ARPCE, en tant qu’autorité de régulati: ARPCE, as the regulatory authority, plays a central role in supervising this sector. It ensures tariff transparency, service quality, and innovation while encouraging private investment. Algérie Télécom, the historical operator, continues to modernize its fixed and mobile network, with a 500 billion DZD investment planned by 2028 for the deployment of fiber optics and the expansion of 5G. Operators Mobilis SA, Djezzy, and Ooredoo are heavily investing in strengthening their infrastructures to meet demand, with combined annual budgets exceeding 200 billion DZD. The 2030 Digital Plan, adopted in 2023, sets clear objectives: to generalize high-speed internet access across all wilayas by 2030 and achieve a 5G coverage rate of 80% of the territory.
Le ministre de la Poste et des Télécommu: The Minister of Post and Telecommunications, Mr. Karim Bibi-Triki, emphasized the importance of this operation in an official press release: "Network stability is a strategic issue for Algeria, both economically and socially. We are counting on the responsiveness of operators to guarantee optimal connectivity during the summer season, in order to support tourism and digital services." The CEO of Mobilis SA, Mr. Abdelkader Bensalah, stated: "We have mobilized additional resources to strengthen our infrastructures in priority wilayas, with special attention to coastal areas. Our goal is to maintain a level of service that meets the expectations of citizens and tourists." Meanwhile, the General Manager of Ooredoo Algeria, Mr. Slimane Ben Slimane, indicated that "dedicated teams will be deployed to monitor the state of the networks in real time and intervene quickly if necessary."
Cette opération de prévention s’inscrit: This preventive operation is part of a broader schedule to strengthen telecom infrastructures in Algeria. By the end of the summer of 2026, a comprehensive evaluation of the implemented measures will be carried out by ARPCE, in collaboration with the operators. The results will serve as a basis for adjusting future strategies, particularly within the framework of the 2030 Digital Plan. Furthermore, a follow-up meeting is scheduled for August 15, 2026, to review intermediate progress and identify any potential additional needs in terms of investments or regulations.
À plus long terme, les autorités algérie: In the longer term, the Algerian authorities aim to make Algeria a regional telecommunications hub, capitalizing on its strategic geographical position and the quality of its infrastructure. The next steps include finalizing agreements for the deployment of 5G in major cities by the end of 2026 and expanding 4G+ services in wilayas that are still poorly served. The widespread rollout of fiber optics in urban and suburban areas is also planned for 2027, with a target of covering 60% of the territory.
